name: Question 14
worked_solution:
Here, $A$ is $3\times 1$ matrix and $B$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in matrix $A$ and $1$ row in matrix $B$, so the product is well defined:

$$
{A}_{3\times \boxed{\text{1}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{B}_{\boxed{\text{1}}\times 2}={AB}_{3\times 2}
$$

Computing the product, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0\cdot 1 & 0\cdot 2 \\ (-2)\cdot 1 & (-2)\cdot 2 \\ (-3)\cdot 1 & (-3)\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & -4 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find AB, if A=[0−2−3] and B=[12].

a
[12−2−4−3−6]
b
[00−2−43−6]
c
[10−2−4−3−6]
d
Undefined
e
[00−2−4−3−6]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, A is 3×1 matrix and B is a 1×2 matrix.

There is 1 column in matrix A and 1 row in matrix B, so the product is well defined:

A3×1⋅✓B1×2=AB3×2

Computing the product, we have:

AB=[0−2−3][12]=[0⋅10⋅2(−2)⋅1(−2)⋅2(−3)⋅1(−3)⋅2]=[00−2−4−3−6]
